title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 5 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Chronicles chapter 5 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 5 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Chronicles Chapter 5.

questions.question: Who was the firstborn of Israel whose birthright was given to the sons of Joseph?
questions.correctAnswer: Reuben
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:1 states that Reuben was the firstborn of Israel, but his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph because he defiled his father's bed.

questions.question: Which tribe prevailed above his brethren and from whom came the chief ruler?
questions.correctAnswer: Judah
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:2 says Judah prevailed above his brethren, and from him came the chief ruler.

questions.question: Who were the sons of Reuben mentioned in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, Carmi
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:3 lists the sons of Reuben as Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.

questions.question: Who was the son of Joel?
questions.correctAnswer: Shemaiah
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:4 identifies Shemaiah as the son of Joel.

questions.question: Which king of Assyria carried away Beerah, prince of the Reubenites, captive?
questions.correctAnswer: Tilgathpilneser
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:6 states that Tilgathpilneser king of Assyria carried away Beerah captive.

questions.question: True or False: The genealogy of the Reubenites is reckoned after the birthright.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:1 clearly says the genealogy is not to be reckoned after the birthright.

questions.question: Where did Bela, son of Azaz, dwell?
questions.correctAnswer: Aroer
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:8 says Bela dwelt in Aroer, even unto Nebo and Baalmeon.

questions.question: True or False: The land eastward inhabited by the Reubenites extended to the river Euphrates.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:9 states they inhabited eastward unto the entering in of the wilderness from the river Euphrates.

questions.question: Why did the Reubenites inhabit the land eastward unto the wilderness from the river Euphrates?
options: Because their cattle were multiplied in the land of Gilead
Because it was fertile for crops
Because it was the promised land
questions.correctAnswer: Because their cattle were multiplied in the land of Gilead
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:9 explains that they inhabited this land because their cattle were multiplied there.

questions.question: The sons of Reuben, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh numbered how many valiant men able for war?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:18 states the number was 44,760 men able for war.

questions.question: True or False: In the days of Saul, the Reubenites made war with the Hagarites and dwelt in their tents throughout the east land of Gilead.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:10 states that in Saul's days they made war with the Hagarites and dwelt in their tents throughout the east land of Gilead.

questions.question: Which comes first in the genealogy list given in 1 Chronicles 5:4-7?
questions.correctAnswer: Shemaiah
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:4 lists Shemaiah as the son of Joel, making him the first mentioned in that genealogy section.

questions.question: Who were the chiefs among the brethren of Beerah by their families?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeiel and Zechariah
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:7 identifies Jeiel and Zechariah as chiefs among Beerah's brethren by their families.

questions.question: True or False: The chapter indicates that the genealogy of the Reubenites was reckoned in the days of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:17 says the genealogies were reckoned in the days of Jotham and Jeroboam, but this verse is beyond the first third of the chapter and not in the primary verse range; per instructions, this fact is outside the easy range.

questions.question: Who is listed as the son of Beerah in the genealogy?
options: None, Beerah is the last named
questions.correctAnswer: None, Beerah is the last named
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:6 shows Beerah as the son of Baal with no son named thereafter in this passage.

medium.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 5 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Chronicles Chapter 5 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 5:10, whom did the Israelites make war with in the days of Saul?
questions.correctAnswer: The Hagarites
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:10 explicitly states that in the days of Saul, the Israelites made war with the Hagarites, who fell by their hand.

questions.question: Where did the children of Gad dwell according to 1 Chronicles 5:11?
options: In the land of Bashan unto Salchah
questions.correctAnswer: In the land of Bashan unto Salchah
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:11 states that the children of Gad dwelt over against the Hagarites, specifically in the land of Bashan unto Salchah.

questions.question: Who was the chief among the leaders mentioned in 1 Chronicles 5:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Joel
questions.explanation: Verse 12 names Joel as the chief, followed by Shapham, Jaanai, and Shaphat in Bashan, indicating Joel’s leadership role.

questions.question: Which group is described as 'valiant men, men able to bear buckler and sword, and to shoot with bow, and skilful in war' in 1 Chronicles 5:18?
options: The sons of Reuben, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh
questions.correctAnswer: The sons of Reuben, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh
questions.explanation: Verse 18 clearly describes these groups as valiant men skilled in war who went out to battle, illustrating their military capability.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 5:20 reveal about the reason the Israelites were helped in battle against the Hagarites?
options: Because they cried to God and put their trust in Him
questions.correctAnswer: Because they cried to God and put their trust in Him
questions.explanation: Verse 20 explains that the Israelites were helped because they earnestly cried to God in battle and trusted in Him, showing the importance of faith and reliance on God.

questions.question: How many camels did the Israelites take away from their enemies according to 1 Chronicles 5:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Fifty thousand
questions.explanation: Verse 21 records that the Israelites took away fifty thousand camels, among other livestock, as spoils of war, demonstrating the scale of their victory.

questions.question: What is the significance of the statement in 1 Chronicles 5:22 about the war being 'of God'?
options: Many were slain because God was executing judgment
The Israelites fought without any casualties
The war was won through human strength alone
The war lasted for many years
questions.correctAnswer: Many were slain because God was executing judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 22 states that many fell because the war was of God, indicating that the casualties were part of divine judgment and sovereignty in the conflict.

questions.question: Where did the children of the half tribe of Manasseh dwell as described in 1 Chronicles 5:23?
options: From Bashan unto Baalhermon and Senir, and unto mount Hermon
questions.correctAnswer: From Bashan unto Baalhermon and Senir, and unto mount Hermon
questions.explanation: Verse 23 describes the geographical range of the half tribe of Manasseh, indicating their expansion from Bashan to the regions of Baalhermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.

questions.question: What does the genealogy reckoning in 1 Chronicles 5:17 indicate about the time period of the record?
options: It was during the reigns of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel
At the time of King David
questions.correctAnswer: It was during the reigns of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 17 clearly states that the genealogies were reckoned in the days of these two kings, placing the record in a specific historical context.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 5:16, the descendants dwelt only in Bashan and nowhere else.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 16 states they dwelt in Gilead in Bashan, in her towns, and all the suburbs of Sharon upon their borders, indicating a broader area than just Bashan.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 5:18–20 teach about the importance of faith and prayer in battle?
options: Victory was granted because they trusted God and cried to Him in battle
Victory was due to superior military strategy alone
They won because of their large numbers without prayer
The text does not mention faith or prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Victory was granted because they trusted God and cried to Him in battle
questions.explanation: Verses 18 to 20 show the valiant men going to war and being helped because they prayed and trusted God, emphasizing faith and dependence on God for success.

questions.question: A believer is struggling with trusting God during difficult battles in life. Based on 1 Chronicles 5:20, what biblical truth applies?
options: Crying to God and trusting Him brings help and deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: Crying to God and trusting Him brings help and deliverance
questions.explanation: Verse 20 demonstrates that the Israelites were helped because they cried to God and trusted Him, teaching believers the power of prayer and trust in God during struggles.

questions.question: Who is identified as the chief of the house of their fathers in 1 Chronicles 5:15?
questions.correctAnswer: Ahi
questions.explanation: Verse 15 names Ahi, son of Abdiel, son of Guni, as the chief of the house of their fathers, highlighting his leadership role.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 5:22, the Israelites immediately left the land after the war with the Hagarites.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 22 states they dwelt in their stead until the captivity, indicating they remained in the land after the war for some time.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 5:14, the children of Abihail are descendants of which ancestor?
questions.correctAnswer: Buz
questions.explanation: Verse 14 traces the genealogy of the children of Abihail back to Buz, showing their ancestral lineage.

hard.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 5 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Chronicles Chapter 5.

questions.question: Which peoples did the Israelites make war with according to 1 Chronicles 5:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Hagarites, Jetur, Nephish, and Nodab
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:19 explicitly states they made war with the Hagarites, Jetur, Nephish, and Nodab, showing the enemies they faced in battle.

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 5:20, what reason is given for the Israelites' victory over the Hagarites?
options: They cried to God and put their trust in Him
They made a surprise attack at night
questions.correctAnswer: They cried to God and put their trust in Him
questions.explanation: Verse 20 shows that Israel’s victory was due to divine help because they cried to God in battle and trusted Him, illustrating the theological theme of reliance on God for success.

questions.question: How many camels did the Israelites take from their enemies as spoils of war according to 1 Chronicles 5:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Fifty thousand
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states they took away fifty thousand camels, emphasizing the scale of their victory and the wealth gained.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 5:22, why did many fall slain in this war?
options: Because the war was of God
questions.correctAnswer: Because the war was of God
questions.explanation: Verse 22 indicates the war was divinely sanctioned, thus many fell because God willed it, showing theological interpretation of warfare.

questions.question: Where did the children of the half tribe of Manasseh dwell as described in 1 Chronicles 5:23?
options: From Bashan unto Baalhermon and Senir, and unto mount Hermon
In the land of Canaan only
questions.correctAnswer: From Bashan unto Baalhermon and Senir, and unto mount Hermon
questions.explanation: Verse 23 describes their territory extending from Bashan to Baalhermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon, indicating their territorial expansion.

questions.question: Who are listed as the heads of the house of their fathers in 1 Chronicles 5:24?
options: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, Jahdiel
Saul, David, Solomon, Nathan, Gad, Asaph, Ezra
Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, Aaron, Joshua
Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, Carmi, Joel, Shemaiah, Gog
questions.correctAnswer: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, Jahdiel
questions.explanation: Verse 24 names these men as mighty and famous heads of their families, highlighting leadership within the half tribe of Manasseh.

questions.question: What sin did the people commit leading to their downfall as mentioned in 1 Chronicles 5:25?
options: They went a whoring after the gods of the people of the land
They worshiped the sun and moon
questions.correctAnswer: They went a whoring after the gods of the people of the land
questions.explanation: Verse 25 explains their transgression was idolatry, forsaking their God to serve local pagan gods, which led to their destruction.

questions.question: Which kings did God stir up to carry away the Reubenites, Gadites, and half tribe of Manasseh as described in 1 Chronicles 5:26?
options: Pul king of Assyria and Tilgathpilneser king of Assyria
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and Cyrus king of Persia
Pharaoh king of Egypt and Sennacherib king of Assyria
David king of Israel and Saul king of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Pul king of Assyria and Tilgathpilneser king of Assyria
questions.explanation: Verse 26 records God stirring the spirits of two Assyrian kings, Pul and Tilgathpilneser, to bring captivity upon these tribes, linking divine judgment with historical Assyrian conquests.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 5:22, the Israelites dwelt in their lands only until the captivity.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states they lived in their lands until the captivity, indicating their displacement was a result of the Assyrian exile.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Chronicles 5:20 suggests the Israelites won the battle solely because of their superior numbers and weapons.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 20 specifies that the Israelites were helped because they cried to God and trusted Him, not merely by military strength, emphasizing divine intervention.

questions.question: Which earlier Old Testament passage also describes God stirring the spirit of kings to accomplish His purposes, similar to 1 Chronicles 5:26?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 10:5-6
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:5-6 describes the Assyrian king as an instrument of God's wrath, paralleling 1 Chronicles 5:26 where God stirs Assyrian kings' spirits for judgment.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'war' in 1 Chronicles 5:19, and how does it reflect the chapter's theme?
options: Milchamah, meaning 'armed conflict' or 'battle', reflecting divine-sanctioned warfare
questions.correctAnswer: Milchamah, meaning 'armed conflict' or 'battle', reflecting divine-sanctioned warfare
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'milchamah' signifies physical battle, which in this chapter is depicted as under God's control and judgment, emphasizing the theological dimension of war.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of trusting God in battle found in 1 Chronicles 5:20?
questions.correctAnswer: Ephesians 6:10-18
questions.explanation: Ephesians 6:10-18 describes the spiritual armor and trust in God during spiritual battles, echoing the trust in God for victory described in 1 Chronicles 5:20.

questions.question: What literary device is used in 1 Chronicles 5:18-22 that frames the narrative of war and divine help?
options: Inclusio framing the description of battle and victory
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio framing the description of battle and victory
questions.explanation: Verses 18 and 22 frame the war narrative by introducing valiant men going to war and concluding with dwelling in their lands until captivity, forming an inclusio that emphasizes divine sovereignty in war.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 5:25 develop the theme of covenant faithfulness seen earlier in the Old Testament?
options: By showing that idolatry leads to destruction, reinforcing covenant consequences
By promising a new covenant with Israel
By introducing a new law code
questions.correctAnswer: By showing that idolatry leads to destruction, reinforcing covenant consequences
questions.explanation: Verse 25's mention of transgression and idolatry connects to covenant themes in Exodus and Deuteronomy where unfaithfulness results in judgment.

theological.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 5 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Chronicles Chapter 5 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is demonstrated by the transfer of the birthright from Reuben to Joseph’s sons as described in 1 Chronicles 5:1?
options: God's sovereign judgment overrides natural birth order
The birthright is always given to the eldest son without exception
Reuben retained the birthright despite his sin
Joseph lost his birthright due to disobedience
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereign judgment overrides natural birth order
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 5:1 explains that although Reuben was the firstborn, his birthright was given to Joseph’s sons because Reuben defiled his father's bed. This shows God's sovereign prerogative in assigning blessings beyond natural inheritance, consistent with Romans 9:15-16 where God's mercy and choice are decisive.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly revealed in 1 Chronicles 5:20 when God responds to Israel’s trust and cries in battle?
options: God’s faithfulness to those who trust Him
God’s hiddenness in times of trouble
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness to those who trust Him
questions.explanation: Verse 20 states that God was intreated of them because they put their trust in Him, revealing His faithfulness and responsiveness to His people’s prayers, echoing Psalm 34:17 where God hears and delivers the righteous in distress.

questions.question: How does the defeat of the Hagarites in 1 Chronicles 5:21-22 reflect the doctrine of God’s providential control over history?
options: God orchestrates victory as an act of His sovereign will
Victory is solely due to Israel’s military skill
The enemies were victorious despite Israel’s prayers
God remains neutral in human conflicts
questions.correctAnswer: God orchestrates victory as an act of His sovereign will
questions.explanation: Verses 21-22 explain many were slain because the war was of God, indicating that God controlled the outcome of the battle, demonstrating His providence as seen in Exodus 14:14 where God fights for His people.

questions.question: What theological implication arises from the statement in 1 Chronicles 5:25 about the tribes’ idolatry and God’s judgment?
options: Sin leads to divine discipline and exile
Idolatry is tolerated by God without consequence
Judgment is unrelated to covenant faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to divine discipline and exile
questions.explanation: Verse 25 states they transgressed and worshipped other gods, whom God had destroyed before them, indicating that idolatry leads to God’s judgment and exile, consistent with Deuteronomy 28:15-68 about covenant curses.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 5:18, what does the enumeration of valiant men reveal about the community’s role in God’s purposes?
options: God equips His people physically for His redemptive mission
Physical strength is irrelevant to spiritual victory
Only priests mattered in Israel’s spiritual life
questions.correctAnswer: God equips His people physically for His redemptive mission
questions.explanation: Verse 18 counts 44,760 men skilled in war, showing that God prepared His people with strength and skill for the fulfillment of His covenant promises, paralleling Exodus 17:8-13 where Moses’ raised hands ensured Israel’s victory.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is illustrated by His raising up Assyrian kings to execute judgment in 1 Chronicles 5:26?
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty over earthly rulers
questions.explanation: Verse 26 shows God stirred the spirit of Assyrian kings to carry away the tribes, demonstrating His sovereign control over nations to fulfill His purposes, consistent with Daniel 4:17 where God’s dominion extends over all kingdoms.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight is conveyed by comparing 1 Chronicles 5:1 and 5:25 about sin and covenant blessings?
options: Sin breaks covenant blessings and God justly transfers privileges
Birthright is permanent regardless of conduct
Idolatry has no effect on God’s blessings
God’s blessings are unconditional and unaffected by sin
questions.correctAnswer: Sin breaks covenant blessings and God justly transfers privileges
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows Reuben lost birthright due to sin; verse 25 highlights idolatry leading to judgment. Together they teach that covenant blessings require faithfulness and sin leads to loss, echoing Numbers 14:18 on God’s justice.

questions.question: How do 1 Chronicles 5:20 and 5:22 together illustrate the relationship between prayer, trust, and divine victory?
options: Trust and prayer invoke God’s intervention leading to victory
Victory is random and unrelated to prayer
Trust negates the need for prayer
Divine victory is guaranteed without human trust
questions.correctAnswer: Trust and prayer invoke God’s intervention leading to victory
questions.explanation: Verse 20 shows God answered their cries because they trusted Him; verse 22 states the war was of God leading to victory, teaching the synergy of faith and prayer in God’s deliverance, as in 2 Chronicles 20:15.

questions.question: What does the captivity of the Reubenites as described in 1 Chronicles 5:6 and 5:26 reveal about God’s judgment and mercy?
options: God’s judgment includes exile but preserves identity for future restoration
God abandons His people permanently in exile
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment includes exile but preserves identity for future restoration
questions.explanation: Verse 6 notes Beerah was carried captive; 5:26 records the exile by Assyrians. This shows God’s judgment via exile, yet the genealogies preserve their identity, pointing to future restoration, as in Jeremiah 29:10.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s involvement in ancient wars contradicts His holiness. What does 1 Chronicles 5:21-22 teach about God's role in warfare?
options: God justly directs wars as part of His holy judgment
God is indifferent and uninvolved in battles
God promotes war for personal gain
God approves all human violence indiscriminately
questions.correctAnswer: God justly directs wars as part of His holy judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 21-22 declare the war was of God, many slain because of His judgment, affirming that God’s involvement in war is just and holy, consistent with Exodus 15:3 where God is a warrior executing holy judgment.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 5:9’s detail about cattle multiplication in the land of Gilead relate to God’s providential blessing on His people?
options: God blesses His people with material prosperity for covenant faithfulness
Material wealth is unrelated to God’s blessing
Cattle multiplication indicates human effort alone
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses His people with material prosperity for covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Verse 9 explains cattle multiplied in Gilead, showing God’s providential blessing on the tribe’s agriculture and livestock, reflecting Genesis 12:2 where God promises Abraham material blessing.

questions.question: What is revealed theologically by the leadership structure of the Gadites in 1 Chronicles 5:12-14?
options: God ordains family and tribal leadership for order and governance
Leadership is randomly assigned without divine purpose
The tribe had no recognized leaders
Leadership was based solely on wealth
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains family and tribal leadership for order and governance
questions.explanation: Verses 12-14 list leaders of Gad’s families, indicating divinely-ordained governance structures within tribes, consistent with Numbers 1:4-16 where leaders are appointed for organization and order.

questions.question: What combined theological insight arises from 1 Chronicles 5:10 and 5:19 about Israel’s conflict with eastern peoples?
options: Israel’s military victories were enabled by God to secure the land
Israel conquered solely through their own strength
The eastern peoples defeated Israel regularly
God was indifferent to Israel’s conflicts
questions.correctAnswer: Israel’s military victories were enabled by God to secure the land
questions.explanation: Verse 10 recounts war with Hagarites resulting in victory; verse 19 mentions war with Hagarites, Jetur, Nephish, Nodab. Together they reveal that God enabled Israel’s victories to establish their inheritance, paralleling Joshua 1:3.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by the genealogical reckoning in 1 Chronicles 5:7-8 regarding the tribes of Reuben and Gad?
options: The importance of covenant identity and continuity through genealogy
Genealogy is irrelevant to God’s purposes
Only the Levites were counted in genealogies
questions.correctAnswer: The importance of covenant identity and continuity through genealogy
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 detail genealogies by families, showing the preservation of tribal identity and covenant continuity, important in Israel’s self-understanding, as seen in Ezra 2:59-63.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 5:2 teach about the relationship between leadership and tribe in Israel’s history?
options: Judah prevailed and produced chief rulers, but birthright belonged to Joseph
Reuben was the chief ruler of Israel
Leadership was equally shared by all tribes
questions.correctAnswer: Judah prevailed and produced chief rulers, but birthright belonged to Joseph
questions.explanation: Verse 2 states Judah prevailed and produced chief rulers, yet the birthright was Joseph’s, showing a complex distribution of leadership and blessing in Israel’s history, consistent with Genesis 49:10.
